questions.question: What is the main purpose of an animal having adaptations?
options: To help them survive in their specific environment
To make them look different from other species
To allow them to change their species over time
To help them find human caretakers

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a physical adaptation in an animal?
options: Migrating south for the winter
Having thick fur to stay warm
Hunting only during the night
Huddling together to keep warm

questions.question: What type of adaptation is being nocturnal (active at night)?
options: Physical adaptation
Physiological adaptation
Structural adaptation
Behavioural adaptation

questions.question: Why is high biodiversity important for ecosystems and habitats?
options: It ensures only one strong species survives
It helps to maintain healthy, stable habitats
It reduces the amount of oxygen in the atmosphere
It makes it easier to build roads and cities

questions.question: What does the term 'gene pool' refer to in biology?
options: The total volume of water where aquatic organisms live
The range of DNA and genetic information within a species
A collection of cells stored in a laboratory freezer
The physical traits that develop due to the environment

questions.question: Which of the following is a method used by scientists to maintain biodiversity?
options: Replacing natural forests with single-crop farms
Using gene banks, conservation, and protection zones
Introducing invasive species to new habitats
Harvesting all resources from an ecosystem quickly

questions.question: Why do scientists use sampling to study populations in a habitat?
options: Because they want to collect and keep every single organism
Because it would be impossible to count every individual organism in a large area
Because sampling is more accurate than counting the actual population
Because organisms only appear when scientists use sampling tools

questions.question: What are quadrats, and what are they used to sample?
options: Long nets used to capture fast-flying birds and insects
Square frames used to sample plants or slow-moving animals
Glass jars used to collect soil and water microbes
Electronic sensors used to track animal migration routes

questions.question: Why is it important that quadrat sampling is usually done randomly?
options: To make sure the scientists can choose the most interesting areas
To avoid bias and get a representative set of results
To ensure that only the rarest plants are counted
To speed up the process so less data is collected

questions.question: What scientific tool is designed to help identify different species based on their characteristics?
options: A classification key
A quadrat frame
A weighing scale
A gene bank database

questions.question: What is an ecosystem made up of?
options: Only the non-living things in a specific area like rocks and water
Only the plants that grow in a particular type of soil
A community of organisms interacting with each other and their non-living surroundings
A single species of animal living in isolation from other living things

questions.question: Organisms in an ecosystem are 'interdependent'. What does this mean?
options: They can survive completely on their own without any other organisms
They depend upon each other for the resources they need to survive
They belong to the exact same species and share DNA
They only compete and never help or rely on one another

questions.question: Why do all living organisms depend on decomposers?
options: They are the primary source of food at the start of all food chains
They break down dead organisms and recycle useful substances for reuse
They hunt predators to keep prey populations under control
They convert sunlight directly into sugar for plants to use

questions.question: What does 'biodiversity' measure?
options: The total mass of all living things in a habitat
The range of different living organisms in an area
The rate of reproduction in a single animal species
The amount of non-living material in an ecosystem

questions.question: Which of the following is a physical adaptation of a plant?
options: Growing roots deeper or shallower, and having spines to deter consumers
Dropping leaves only when touched by a human
Bending towards a window to receive more sunlight
Releasing seeds only during the night

questions.question: Which of these is a behavioural adaptation in plants?
options: Having a waxy coating on leaves
Growing towards light
Developing long, deep taproots
Growing sharp thorns on stems

questions.question: What is biomass?
options: The total number of individual organisms in an ecosystem
The mass of living material in one or more organisms
The speed at which energy passes through a food chain
The weight of the non-living parts of a habitat

questions.question: What does a pyramid of biomass show?
options: The total population size of each species in an area
The biomass of organisms at each stage in a food chain
The speed of decomposition of organic material
The amount of water stored in different trophic levels

questions.question: Where is the producer always located in a pyramid of biomass?
options: At the very top of the pyramid
In the middle of the pyramid
At the bottom of the pyramid
It is excluded from the pyramid

questions.question: What is represented in a pyramid of number?
options: The total dry weight of organisms at each level
The number of organisms at each trophic level in a food chain
The amount of energy lost as heat at each level
The number of different species in the entire ecosystem
